Subject: Re: sudden latency spike during morning batch windows

Quick summary from infra triage (initial):
- Observed: increased init/warmup latency on GPU pool nodes during autoscale wake. Median wake time increased from ~2.2s to ~6.1s; p99 spikes to 9–14s in the affected window.
- Correlated with a kernel module update and a change in container image layering we shipped three days ago (smaller images, layered caching). We pushed a new image builder that altered the order of runtime libraries; it appears to trigger extra driver initialization paths on certain NIC/driver combos.
- Repro: local repro playback on a staging customer cluster reproduced the p99 when using the newer image layering and cold container start.

Short mitigations we can apply immediately:
1) Force-route Clearwater to a warm standby pool (pre-warmed instances) while we patch — low-risk, quick to do (5–15m to flip).
2) Temporarily revert the image layering change for hostedapi pools serving Clearwater until we validate a fix (rolling revert, ~1h including canary).
3) Apply a runtime init timeout and a fallback to a lighter model variant for the first request to avoid long-tail blocking (~2–4h to roll with testing).

We’ll push an emergency canary of the revert to a small subset in the next 45m and report back. I’m attaching host logs and a repro playback.

—Dylan
Staff Software Engineer, Infra

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency spike during morning batch windows — exec summary and actions

Exec summary for customer/comms:
- Impact: Clearwater experienced p95 regression from ~850ms to ~4s and p99 up to ~11s during autoscaler wake; incident window ~2026-11-01T15:55:00–2026-11-01T16:30:00 PST. Throughput for a critical job dropped ~30%.
- Root cause (initial): recent container image layering change + kernel module interaction causing extra driver init on cold start (affects subset of NIC/hypervisor combos).

Immediate actions (we will execute now):
1) Route Clearwater traffic to a pre-warmed dedicated standby pool (estimate: 15 minutes to complete).
2) Roll back image layering change for Hosted API pools serving Clearwater (canary 10% in 20m; full roll 60–90m after validation).
3) Deploy a temporary runtime fast-fail for driver init >7s and fallback to a lighter model on first request (estimated 2–4 hours to safely deploy).
4) Postmortem and permanent fix (kernel-driver-safe image build) to be delivered in 5 business days with test coverage and staged canaries.

Customer compensation recommendation: 10–20% service credit for the affected billing period for the customer-facing reconciliation throughput drop and operational impact. I authorize Marissa to negotiate within that band.

I’ll join the customer call if requested. Please confirm when routing is complete and provide canary telemetry.

—Aditya
VP, Platform Infrastructure
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Update and next steps (routing + timeline)

Priya — thanks again for the quick signal and the CSV. Quick update:
- We routed your workload to a pre-warmed standby pool at 2026-11-01T17:05:00 PST; you should see p95/p99 return to normal for new requests.
- We started a canary rollback of the image layering change to 10% at 2026-11-01T17:20:00 PST and expanded to 100% at 2026-11-01T18:10:00 PST after validation.
- We will deploy a runtime fast-fail + lighter-variant fallback today; target completion within 4 hours.

Next steps for Clearwater:
1) We plan a short incident review and root-cause writeup by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-03).
2) Marissa will follow up on the service credit proposal (we recommend 15% for the affected billing period; open to discussion).
3) If you’re available, Aditya and Dylan can join a 30m call today at 11:00 PST to walk through the technical details and confirm mitigations.

Please let me know if routing to the warm pool fully removed the failures on your side. We’ll keep this thread for the postmortem and timeline.

Best,
Sofia
